make.name: Hyundai
make.description: South Korean carmaker and one of the world's largest. Its Ioniq sub-brand (Ioniq 5, 6, 9) uses the 800-volt E-GMP platform; it also sells the Kona Electric, Inster and market-specific EVs in China and India.

models.name: BlueOn
models.description: Hyundai's first battery-electric car, a small hatchback based on the i10 and unveiled in 2010. It was built in very small numbers, mainly for field testing by South Korean government agencies.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: i10-based prototype-series EV with a 16.4 kWh lithium-polymer pack and about 140 km of range.

models.name: Ioniq Electric
models.description: Battery-electric version of the Ioniq liftback, sold alongside hybrid and plug-in hybrid versions. Launched in 2016 with a 28 kWh pack, updated in 2019 with a 38.3 kWh pack; Ioniq production ended in July 2022.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 28 kWh pack, 88-89 kW motor; EPA-rated 124 miles.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Bigger 38.3 kWh pack and 100 kW motor; EPA range rose to 170 miles. US sales ended after model year 2021.

models.name: Kona Electric
models.description: Subcompact electric crossover. The first generation (2018) offered 39 and 64 kWh packs; the larger second generation arrived in 2023. In China the first generation was sold as the Encino EV, and in India it was replaced by the Creta Electric in 2024.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original Kona-based EV with a 39.2 kWh (Europe/Korea) or 64 kWh pack; the US got only the 64 kWh version.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Restyled nose (unveiled September 2020) on the same 39.2 / 64 kWh hardware.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Larger, EV-first redesign with 48.6 kWh (Standard Range) and 64.8 kWh (Long Range) packs. Hyundai skipped the 2026 model year in the US, calling it a pause.

models.name: Ioniq 5
models.description: Retro-styled compact electric crossover on Hyundai's 800-volt E-GMP platform, launched in 2021. A 2024 facelift (US model year 2025) brought a bigger 84 kWh pack, a native NACS port in the US and the rugged XRT trim.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version with a 58 kWh Standard Range or 77.4 kWh Long Range pack and RWD or dual-motor AWD.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Bigger packs (63 / 84 kWh), restyled bumpers, a native NACS port in the US, and the off-road-styled XRT.

models.name: Ioniq 5 N
models.description: High-performance version of the Ioniq 5 from Hyundai's N division, with dual motors, 84 kWh pack, simulated gearshifts and a boost mode up to 641 hp. Hyundai cut the US price by $6,300 for model year 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 84 kWh, dual-motor AWD; 601 hp normally and 641 hp with N Grin Boost.

models.name: Ioniq 6
models.description: Streamlined E-GMP sedan launched in 2022. A facelift arrived in 2025 with an 84 kWh pack, but Hyundai dropped the standard Ioniq 6 from the US starting with the 2026 model year; only the Ioniq 6 N continues there.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version with 53 kWh Standard Range or 77.4 kWh Long Range packs, RWD or dual-motor AWD.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Restyled nose and tail, 84 kWh pack. Sold in Europe, the UK and Korea, not in the US.

models.name: Ioniq 6 N
models.description: Performance sedan from Hyundai N, revealed in July 2025, with dual motors, 84 kWh pack and up to 641 hp in boost mode. On sale in the UK; Hyundai says it will reach the US in limited numbers, where it is the only Ioniq 6 left.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Based on the facelifted Ioniq 6 with N chassis, aero and the Ioniq 5 N's dual-motor drivetrain.

models.name: Ioniq 9
models.description: Three-row electric SUV on E-GMP with a 110.3 kWh pack, built in Georgia (US) and Korea. Launched in 2025 as a 2026 model.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Single-motor RWD, dual-motor AWD and a 422 hp Performance AWD, all with 110.3 kWh.

models.name: Inster
models.description: Small electric crossover-hatch derived from the Korean Casper, sold as the Casper Electric in Korea and as the Inster in Europe and elsewhere. Offered with 42 or 49 kWh packs.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-motor city EV with 42 kWh (97 PS) or 49 kWh (115 PS) packs.

models.name: Ioniq 3
models.description: Compact 'aero hatch' revealed at Milan Design Week in April 2026 and built in Izmit, Turkey, for Europe. Offered with 42.2 and 61 kWh packs on a 400-volt platform.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version; production started in August 2026.

models.name: Elexio
models.description: Compact electric SUV developed for China and built by the Beijing Hyundai joint venture, with BYD (FinDream) LFP batteries. Launched in October 2025, also sold as the EO.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 64.2 or 88.1 kWh LFP packs, front motor or dual-motor AWD; CLTC range 518-722 km depending on version.

models.name: Ioniq V
models.description: China-only electric sedan designed by Hyundai's China team, with CATL LFP batteries and Momenta driver assistance. Launched on 29 September 2026 at 109,900-139,900 yuan.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Two LFP packs: 53.5 kWh (CLTC 540 km) and 66.8 kWh (CLTC 650 km).

models.name: Creta Electric
models.description: Electric version of India's best-selling Creta SUV, launched at the Auto Expo in January 2025 with 42 and 51.4 kWh packs. It replaced the Kona Electric in India.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-motor EV; MIDC range 390 km (42 kWh) and 473 km (51.4 kWh) at launch.

models.name: Staria Electric
models.description: Battery-electric version of the Staria people mover, with an 84 kWh pack and 800-volt charging. Sales started in Korea and Europe in 2026; a Staria Load cargo van version is also offered.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-wheel-drive, 160 kW motor, 84 kWh pack.

models.name: Lafesta EV
models.description: Electric version of the China-market Lafesta sedan, built by Beijing Hyundai with a 56.5 kWh CATL pack. Sold from late 2019; the electric version was listed until 2022.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 56.5 kWh pack, 310 Nm motor, NEDC range 490 km.

models.name: Mistra EV
models.description: Electric version of the second-generation Mistra sedan for China, shown at the 2020 Guangzhou show and sold from 2021. The generation ended in 2023.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: 56.5 kWh pack, NEDC range 520 km.

models.name: Neira
models.description: Seven-seat electric MPV for Indonesia, unveiled at GIIAS 2026 as a rebadged Kia Carens Clavis EV, to be built at Hyundai's Cikarang plant. Specs and price are not yet official.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Pre-production; Hyundai has not published specifications.

legacy_notes.note: Labelled 'Limited (1st Gen)' but its image (hyundai_kona_ltd.png) shows the second-generation Kona Electric, and its 188 lb-ft torque is the second-gen figure. Claimed on the first-gen 64 kWh variant.
Second-gen Kona Electric Limited: price 34,470 is the 2025 SE price including destination, not the Limited. Same hardware as SEL (row 112), so both are claimed on the Long Range variant.
Labelled 2025 facelift Limited AWD but 318 mi is the RWD EPA range (AWD is 290/269 mi), price 43,975 matches no Limited AWD price, and the image ioniq5_ltd_awd.png shows the pre-facelift car.
Pre-facelift Limited AWD, but stored generation is '2025 Facelift'. Claimed on the 2022 original-generation Long Range AWD.
Disney100 Platinum Edition is a 2024 limited edition of the pre-facelift Limited AWD; not a distinct configuration.
image_url /pub_assets/car_images/ioniq5_sel_rwd.png does not exist; the file on disk is ioniq5_sel_rwd.png.png, so this card shows a broken image.
Ioniq 6 Limited AWD price 37,750 is actually the base SE Standard Range price; Limited AWD launched at 56,100 (2023). Standard Ioniq 6 is no longer sold in the US from model year 2026.
Ioniq 6 SE RWD: 361 mi is the 2023-24 rating; 2025 SE RWD is 342 mi.

gaps: Kona Electric US: Hyundai skipped model year 2026 and said 2027 production would start in June 2026; could not confirm 2027 US pricing or on-sale status (web search budget ran out), so US status is left 'current'.
Ioniq 6 N: no official US price yet; EPA lists a 2027 Ioniq 6 N at 245 mi. US market left 'upcoming'.
Ioniq 9 US connector not sourced; EU prices and WLTP per variant not filled.
Elexio: battery-to-version mapping and official price not found; ranges only described in generation text.
Ioniq 3: power published only as kW/PS (107.8 kW / 99.5 kW), so power_hp left null; drivetrain and top speed not filled (sources disagree on top speed); UK price for 61 kWh only implied.
Ioniq 6 facelift and Ioniq 9 UK ranges are published in miles (WLTP); left null because WLTP must be stored in km and conversion is not allowed.
Commercial EVs not included: Porter II Electric, ST1, Staria Load (cargo), Elec City bus.
Lafesta EV power differs between sources (135 kW vs 150 kW); left null.
Older US prices (Ioniq Electric 2020, Kona Electric 2020-2023, Ioniq 6 2024) not sourced.
